sports.image_caption: Ravichandran Ashwin in bowling action during a Test match at Trent Bridge in 2018

sports.image_caption: Estadio Azteca in Mexico City, dressed for the 2026 FIFA World Cup
sports.nri_angle: NRIs across North America are experiencing the World Cup in their own cities — Houston, New Jersey, the Bay Area — making the Round of 16 feel local for the first time.

sports.nri_angle: NRI cricket fans in the UK are watching the Sooryavanshi debut saga unfold at English grounds they have historically filled — and many are desperate to see the teenage prodigy unleashed.

technology.title: Apple Tells India Its Antitrust Case Was 'Copy-Pasted.' The Fine Could Hit $38 Billion.
technology.excerpt: In its sharpest legal filing yet, Apple accuses the CCI of recycling rivals' complaints rather than conducting independent analysis — but India's regulators have heard that argument before, from Google.
technology.image_caption: Aerial view of Apple Park in Cupertino, California — headquarters of a company now facing up to $38 billion in antitrust exposure in India
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin iOS developers and fintech founders on both sides of the Pacific could see fundamental changes to how the App Store operates in India, while PhonePe — widely used by NRIs for cross-border payments — is among the complainants.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Is Building 20 AI Models to Rival ChatGPT. Its Strategy Is to Skip the Arms Race.
technology.excerpt: As the US restricts its most powerful AI systems, India is funding homegrown open-source models that deliver 60-80% of frontier capability — and betting that's enough for most of the world.
technology.image_caption: A modern data center server unit — the infrastructure India is racing to build for its sovereign AI ambitions
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin AI researchers at Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic now have open-source Indian models to build on, while NRI investors get exposure to a government-backed AI ecosystem producing tangible outputs.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Companies Spending the Most on AI Are Hiring the Fastest. The Full Story Is More Complicated.
technology.excerpt: A new study of 22,000 companies finds heavy AI adopters grew headcount 10%. But 185,000 tech workers lost jobs this year, and Indians on H-1B are the most exposed population of all.
technology.image_caption: An illustration of artificial intelligence and machine learning — the technology reshaping both hiring and layoff patterns across Silicon Valley
technology.nri_angle: Indians hold the largest share of H-1B visas and are disproportionately affected by AI-driven layoffs, while senior Indian engineers are increasingly pursuing EB-1A green cards to decouple their immigration status from volatile employers.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: OpenAI's New India Chief Is an IIT-IIM Alum Who Ran Uber for a Decade
technology.excerpt: Prabhjeet Singh, who expanded Uber across India and South Asia for 11 years, will lead OpenAI's second-largest market. He starts in September.
technology.image_caption: OpenAI headquarters at the Pioneer Building in San Francisco. Credit: Wikimedia Commons
technology.nri_angle: An IIT Kharagpur and IIM Ahmedabad alumnus now leads OpenAI's India strategy — a signal that the AI labs are drawing from the same elite Indian talent pipeline as FAANG, with product decisions increasingly shaped by India's 100 million ChatGPT users.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's Agnikul Just Signed a Deal to Launch Radar Satellites. The Partner Is Finnish.
technology.excerpt: Agnikul Cosmos and Finland's ICEYE will build sovereign SAR satellite capabilities in India, announced at the Bharat Innovates summit with Modi and Macron present.
technology.image_caption: ISRO LVM3 rocket on its launch pad in India. Credit: ISRO/Wikimedia Commons
technology.nri_angle: India's private space sector is becoming a real investment and career proposition for NRIs in aerospace — Agnikul's $500M valuation and sovereign SAR satellite deal represent both return-to-India pathways and cross-border business opportunities.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Google Just Gave Its AI Agent a Desktop. It Costs $100 a Month and It Wants Your Files.
technology.excerpt: Gemini Spark launched on macOS with third-party integrations, real-time tracking, and an Indian-origin DeepMind VP leading the engineering. The desktop agent war is on.
technology.image_caption: Google CEO Sundar Pichai at a public event in 2023
technology.nri_angle: An Indian-origin VP of Engineering at Google DeepMind co-leads the Gemini Spark launch. For millions of Indian tech professionals using Google Workspace, the choice of desktop AI agent is becoming as consequential as the choice of operating system a decade ago.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: SK Hynix Is Coming to Nasdaq on July 10. Mehrotra's Micron Just Lost Its American Monopoly.
technology.excerpt: The South Korean chipmaker that dominates high-bandwidth memory plans a $29 billion ADR listing — arriving on the same exchange as Micron, and directly in the sightlines of every NRI portfolio that rode the AI memory trade.
technology.image_caption: Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra at a 2025 event
technology.nri_angle: NRI investors who bet on Micron for its Indian CEO and Gujarat fab now face a second memory stock on Nasdaq that could split passive index flows and compress Micron's valuation premium.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Apple Is Lobbying Washington to Buy Chips from a Blacklisted Chinese Company. The Price Tag Explains Why.
technology.excerpt: Memory costs are soaring so fast that Apple raised Mac and iPad prices by up to 25 per cent — and is now asking the Trump administration for clearance to source DRAM from CXMT, a Chinese chipmaker on the Pentagon's military-linked list.
technology.image_caption: Apple CEO Tim Cook — the company is lobbying Washington to allow purchases from blacklisted Chinese chipmaker YMTC (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: The AI memory crunch affects every NRI in tech — from Micron's Gujarat fab and Indian chip ambitions to the iPhone 18 pricing that hits every consumer's wallet.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: The World's Central Bankers Just Held a Meeting. Every Conversation Was About AI.
technology.excerpt: At the ECB's annual Sintra forum, the architects of global monetary policy compared the AI investment boom to the dotcom crash and the railway mania of the 1840s. For NRI tech workers and investors, the warning is personal.
technology.image_caption: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh at the ECB Sintra forum, where he called the AI revolution the biggest economic event of our lifetime
technology.nri_angle: Indian H-1B workers make up 70 per cent of US tech visa holders and NRI portfolios are heavily concentrated in AI stocks — both are directly exposed if central bankers are right about an AI-driven correction.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: A Noida Kid's BASIC Program Led to an $8.3 Billion AI Company. Together AI Just Raised $800 Million.
technology.excerpt: Vipul Ved Prakash's open-source cloud platform, backed by Aramco, Nvidia and Salesforce, is becoming the infrastructure layer the AI industry didn't know it needed.
technology.image_caption: Vipul Ved Prakash, co-founder and CEO of Together AI
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin founder from Noida builds $8.3B AI infrastructure company; platform enables affordable AI for Indian startups like Sarvam AI and Krutrim; major hiring pipeline from Indian engineering talent.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Meta Is Building a Cloud Business. The Neoclouds It Hired Are Already Bleeding.
technology.excerpt: Zuckerberg's company plans to sell excess AI computing capacity, sending CoreWeave and Nebius stocks into freefall and reshaping the cloud landscape Indian IT firms depend on.
technology.image_caption: Meta headquarters in Menlo Park, California — the company is building a cloud computing business to rent out AI infrastructure (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: Thousands of Indian engineers work at Meta and neocloud firms facing strategic upheaval; Indian IT services giants (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) may need to build expertise around a fourth hyperscaler; cheaper AI compute benefits Indian startups.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: The US Government Froze Anthropic's Best AI for 17 Days. Then It Unfroze It. The Damage Was Already Done.
technology.excerpt: Export controls on Claude Fable 5 locked out foreign-national employees — including Indian engineers — and threw a trillion-dollar IPO into doubt. The ban is lifted. The precedent is not.
technology.image_caption: Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, at TechCrunch Disrupt
technology.nri_angle: Indian AI researchers on H-1B visas were locked out of their own models at Anthropic; episode exposes a new regulatory risk for Indian professionals at frontier AI labs; India's own AI governance framework must account for this kind of precedent.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Nestlé Will Strip Artificial Colourings From Every Product on Earth by Year-End — and It Could Reshape What Indians Eat
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The Swiss food giant becomes the first major packaged-food company to set a global deadline for eliminating synthetic dyes, a move driven by GLP-1 drug pressure and RFK Jr.'s FDA crackdown that could ripple through Maggi, KitKat, and Munch in India
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Nestlé products on a supermarket shelf — the company plans to remove all artificial colourings from its global portfolio by end-2026
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRIs navigating different food safety standards between the US/UK and India may finally see consistency as Nestlé standardises its ingredient lists globally — including for iconic Indian brands like Maggi and KitKat
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Simultaneous Heat Emergency Is Scorching Two Continents — and Millions of Indian Diaspora Are in Its Path
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Europe's deadliest heatwave in years has killed over 1,300 people, and now a punishing heat dome is descending on the US for July 4th. For the 7 million-strong Indian diaspora across both regions, the message is the same: this is not normal summer heat.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Extreme heat conditions — a simultaneous heatwave is affecting both the United States and South Asia (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Over 6 million Indian-origin residents in the US and UK face record-breaking heat in their home cities, with multigenerational households and elderly family members at acute risk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A New Weight-Loss Drug Just Matched Bariatric Surgery — and It Could Change How South Asians Fight Obesity
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Eli Lilly's retatrutide produced 28% weight loss at 80 weeks in the landmark TRIUMPH-1 trial, the first medication ever to rival surgical outcomes — a potential game-changer for a community with the world's highest metabolic disease burden.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An Ozempic injection pen — retatrutide belongs to the same GLP-1 drug class but targets three metabolic receptors instead of one
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry the world's highest metabolic disease burden relative to BMI — a drug matching bariatric surgery outcomes could transform obesity treatment for the diaspora.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Weedkiller in Your Food May Be Rewiring Your Brain Through Your Gut — and the 'Safe' Doses Aren't So Safe
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A wave of new research finds glyphosate — sprayed on wheat, oats, lentils, and most American crops — disrupts gut bacteria, alters brain chemistry, and triggers anxiety-like behavior at doses far below regulatory limits
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Agricultural spraying in a crop field — glyphosate is the world's most widely used herbicide
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRIs face high glyphosate exposure through the American food supply — and India's own use of the herbicide on tea, wheat, and lentils means the risk cuts across both food systems
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Medicare Will Now Cover Ozempic and Wegovy for Weight Loss — Here's Who Qualifies and What It Costs
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new pilot program launching July 1 lets eligible seniors get GLP-1 drugs for just $50 a month, but the fine print matters — and the clock is already ticking.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An Ozempic (semaglutide) injection pen — Medicare will now cover GLP-1 medications for weight loss (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated metabolic risk at lower BMI thresholds, and many NRI families are navigating Medicare coverage for aging parents — making this program particularly relevant for multigenerational Indian American households.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: South Asians Have the Highest Heart Disease Risk at 45 — Despite Eating Better and Drinking Less Than Everyone Else
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A decade-long study of 2,700 U.S. adults found that South Asian men and women develop prediabetes, hypertension, and high cholesterol earlier than every other racial group — even though they report healthier diets and lower alcohol use. The researchers say visceral fat and early-life exposures may explain the paradox.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A doctor checks blood pressure during a cardiovascular screening — researchers say South Asians should begin heart health screenings before midlife
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian Americans face the highest cardiovascular risk of any U.S. racial group by age 45 — a finding that demands earlier screening, lipoprotein(a) testing, and culturally tailored care for the diaspora community.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Walking 10,000 Steps a Day Can Offset a Full Day at Your Desk, a 72,000-Person Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Researchers at the University of Sydney found that each increase in daily steps — up to about 10,000 — was linked to a 39% lower risk of death and 21% lower risk of heart disease, regardless of how many hours participants spent sitting. For the millions of South Asian tech workers who log 8-plus hours at a desk, the data offers a clear prescription.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Walking remains the most accessible countermeasure to prolonged sitting, with benefits scaling up to about 10,000 steps per day
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian tech workers in the U.S. spend 8-10 hours at desks — among the highest sedentary rates of any demographic — and already face elevated cardiovascular risk by midlife. Walking 10,000 steps daily can meaningfully offset the damage.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Americans Are Ditching Multivitamins for Targeted Supplements — and Two of the Fastest-Growing Are Ayurvedic Staples
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A 25-year JAMA analysis of 63,000 adults finds supplement use surging while multivitamin use drops — with turmeric and ashwagandha leading the charge
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Assorted dietary supplements including vitamin D, magnesium, and turmeric capsules
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Turmeric and ashwagandha — Ayurvedic staples in South Asian households — are now among America's fastest-growing supplements, while targeted vitamin D matters disproportionately for NRIs at higher latitudes.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The FDA Just Cleared an AI Tool That Detects Hidden Heart Disease From a Routine ECG — and South Asians May Benefit Most
lifestyle-health.excerpt: EchoNext, trained on 700,000 ECG records, caught severe heart failure a cardiologist missed — and its clearance could reshape screening for high-risk populations
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An electrocardiogram readout showing heart rhythm patterns
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face 2-4x higher coronary disease rates and often develop heart disease a decade earlier — an AI tool that reads hidden cardiac risk from routine ECGs could catch disease years before symptoms appear.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Strength Training Cuts Type 2 Diabetes Risk by Up to 62% — and Consistency Matters More Than Intensity
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A study of nearly 144,000 people over 19 years found that regular weight training — especially when combined with cardio and less screen time — offers powerful diabetes protection that South Asians have extra reason to pay attention to.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A woman performing strength training exercises in a gym studio
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians are genetically predisposed to insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes at lower BMIs — making the case for strength training even more urgent for the diaspora.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Gut Bacteria May Reveal Colorectal Cancer Before Symptoms Appear — and Fiber Could Be the Key to Prevention
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new study in Cell Host & Microbe has identified a consistent microbial signature linked to colorectal cancer across ages and populations — and lower fiber intake made it worse.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Illustration of the human gut microbiome, increasingly linked to colorectal cancer detection and prevention (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Colorectal cancer rates are surging among young adults globally, and NRIs shifting from fiber-rich Indian diets to Western ultra-processed food face particular risk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: GLP-1 Drugs Like Ozempic Are Now Linked to Smell and Taste Disturbances — and the Implications Go Beyond Food
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A study of nearly 900,000 diabetes patients found that GLP-1 users had an 81% higher risk of smell dysfunction and a 52% higher risk of taste changes — subtle shifts that doctors say are early markers of neurological health.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A semaglutide injection pen — GLP-1 receptor agonists like Ozempic are now linked to smell and taste disturbances in a growing body of research (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians have among the highest GLP-1 prescription rates due to elevated type 2 diabetes prevalence, and sensory loss carries outsized cultural weight in communities where food is central to identity.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Chicken Stock in Dal Makhani? A Former MasterChef Judge Just Ignited Indian Food's Loudest Fight
food.excerpt: George Calombaris's Instagram reel adding chicken stock cubes to dal makhani has reignited the perennial debate over who gets to reinterpret Indian classics — and where the red line sits.
food.image_caption: A bowl of traditional dal makhani garnished with cream and fresh coriander
food.nri_angle: For NRIs who grew up eating their mother's dal makhani, the controversy touches a nerve about cultural ownership and whether Western chefs dilute Indian food's identity as it goes global.

food.title: From a Hotel Lobby in Fort Collins to a Strip Mall in Columbus: Indian Food Is Showing Up Everywhere
food.excerpt: A new wave of Indian restaurants is quietly spreading into mid-sized American cities far from the coastal corridors, driven by immigrant families betting on untapped appetites.
food.image_caption: A spread of Indian dishes including dosa, curry, and chutney served on a restaurant table
food.nri_angle: For NRIs living outside traditional desi enclaves, these openings signal that Indian food is becoming accessible in the kinds of cities where finding a decent biryani once meant a two-hour drive.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Tandoori on the Grill: How the Desi Fourth of July Became a Diaspora Tradition
food.excerpt: This Independence Day, Indian Americans are bringing tikka marinades, masala corn, and chutney sliders to the backyard cookout — reshaping what the all-American BBQ looks like

food.title: The Beard's New Palate: Indian Cuisine's Record Run at America's Most Prestigious Food Awards
food.excerpt: From Chai Pani to Tamba to Cal-India Collective, a record number of South Asian finalists at the 2026 James Beard Awards signals a seismic shift in how America eats
food.image_caption: The James Beard Foundation Award medallion — this year, Indian and South Asian chefs competed for it in unprecedented numbers

food.title: Vacuum-Sealed Nostalgia: The Gujarati Home Kitchens Feeding America's NRIs
food.excerpt: In Mumbai and Ahmedabad, a network of women entrepreneurs is vacuum-packing thepla, khakhra, and fafda for suitcase-bound NRIs — and the business is booming
food.image_caption: A traditional Gujarati snack spread — the kind of comfort food that travels thousands of miles in vacuum-sealed packages to NRI doorsteps
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: The Quiet Grocery Conquest: Inside Patel Brothers' Push Into America's Fastest-Growing Suburbs
food.excerpt: From a single Chicago storefront in 1974 to over 50 locations nationwide, the largest Indian grocery chain in America is following the diaspora into suburbs that never had a dal section — and reshaping what neighbourhood grocery stores look like.
food.image_caption: Devon Avenue in Chicago, home to the original Patel Brothers store and one of America's densest concentrations of South Asian commerce (Wikimedia Commons)
food.nri_angle: For NRIs who once drove hours for a packet of Haldiram's or fresh curry leaves, a Patel Brothers opening in their suburb means home has come to them.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Tikka Masala Naan, Bombay Spice Chips, and Beet Tikka Patties: Indian Food Just Swept America's Top Grocery Awards
food.excerpt: Three Indian-inspired brands earned top honours at the 2026 NEXTY Awards — the natural food industry's equivalent of the Oscars — in a year that confirmed Indian cuisine's breakout moment in American retail.
food.image_caption: Freshly baked butter naan served alongside three different Indian curries
food.nri_angle: For NRIs who have spent years explaining what naan is to American colleagues, watching Indian food win mainstream grocery awards feels like vindication — and a sign that the frozen aisle is finally catching up to their kitchens.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: The Air Fryer Rewrote the Samosa: How NRI Kitchens Became 2026's Viral Recipe Labs
food.excerpt: From oil-free samosas racking up 15 million views to jaggery rasmalai tres leches cakes that fuse two continents in a single dessert, the most viral Indian recipes of 2026 are being invented in diaspora kitchens.
food.image_caption: Golden, crispy samosas served as a popular Indian snack
food.nri_angle: NRI kitchens — caught between their mothers' recipes and American appliance culture — have become the unlikely laboratories for the most inventive Indian food content on the internet.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Musaafer's Taj Mahal Comes to Tribeca: Inside New York's Most Opulent Indian Restaurant
food.excerpt: The Houston fine-dining sensation — where lotus chandeliers hang above nihari birria tacos and butter chicken arrives as a two-act experience — opens a lavish second act in lower Manhattan.
food.image_caption: The Tribeca neighbourhood in Manhattan, where Musaafer has opened New York's most opulent Indian restaurant (Wikimedia Commons)
food.nri_angle: For Indian Americans tired of explaining that their food culture extends far beyond chicken tikka masala, Musaafer's state-by-state culinary journey is a showcase of India's staggering diversity.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: The $5 Alphonso: Inside the Mango Vans Rolling Through America's Indian Neighbourhoods
food.excerpt: India's mango exports to the US have already surpassed last year's full-season total, driven by WhatsApp-coordinated delivery vans, surging diaspora demand, and a season extended by northern Indian varieties.
food.image_caption: Fresh Indian Alphonso mangoes, the most sought-after variety among diaspora communities in the US
food.nri_angle: Indian mangoes are a visceral link to home for NRIs — the WhatsApp-driven delivery networks and record exports reflect a diaspora willing to pay a premium for a taste of identity.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: From 7-Eleven to James Beard: The Improbable Rise of Chef Suresh Sundas
food.excerpt: The Nepali-born chef who taught himself to cook in his mother's kitchen has become the first person from Nepal to be named a James Beard Award finalist — and he's rewriting the rules of Indian food in Washington, DC.
food.image_caption: Daru restaurant in Washington DC's H Street corridor, co-founded by Chef Suresh Sundas and Dante Datta
food.nri_angle: Sundas's journey from Nepali immigrant working at 7-Eleven to history-making James Beard finalist embodies the unsung South Asian culinary talent reshaping American dining.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Beyond the Buffet: Indian Food Finally Gets Its Fast-Casual Moment in America
food.excerpt: From Curry Up Now's tikka burritos to Tarka Indian Kitchen's Texas expansion, Indian cuisine is carving out a fast-casual niche that the industry has predicted for years — and this time, the numbers suggest it's real.
food.image_caption: A vibrant Indian thali — the traditional multi-dish platter is being reimagined by a new wave of fast-casual restaurants sweeping across American cities.
food.nri_angle: The fast-casual boom means Indian food — the chaat, kathi rolls, dosas — is finally being presented to mainstream America the way diaspora communities have always known it deserves.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: The Supreme Court Just Saved Birthright Citizenship. No Community Had More at Stake Than Indian Americans.
carousel.excerpt: With green card backlogs stretching past a century, tens of thousands of Indian families in the U.S. faced losing their children's citizenship. The 6-3 ruling shuts that door.
carousel.image_caption: The United States Supreme Court in Washington, D.C.
carousel.nri_angle: Indian families on H-1B and green card backlogs are among those most protected by the ruling, as their U.S.-born children's citizenship was directly threatened by Trump's executive order.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Priyadarshan Lost Hera Pheri 3. So He Called Akshay Kumar Instead.
carousel.excerpt: The director-actor duo who gave us Bhagam Bhag, Garam Masala, and De Dana Dan are reuniting for a comedy thriller that Priyadarshan says he's never attempted before
carousel.image_caption: Akshay Kumar at a film event (Wikimedia Commons)
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Balogun Scored. Then He Was Sent Off. Ten-Man USA Beat Bosnia 2-0 in the Bay Area to Reach the World Cup Round of 16.
carousel.excerpt: Folarin Balogun’s third goal of the tournament and a stunning Malik Tillman free kick powered the Americans past Bosnia at Levi’s Stadium — ending a 24-year wait for a knockout-stage win, with NRIs in Silicon Valley celebrating alongside them.
carousel.image_caption: Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, the Bay Area venue that hosted the USA vs Bosnia World Cup match
carousel.nri_angle: The World Cup Round of 32 match was played at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara — the heart of Silicon Valley — making it a once-in-a-generation live sporting event for Bay Area NRIs, many of whom have adopted American soccer as a second sporting passion.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Apple Tells India Its Antitrust Case Was 'Copy-Pasted.' The Fine Could Hit $38 Billion.
carousel.excerpt: In its sharpest legal filing yet, Apple accuses the CCI of recycling rivals' complaints rather than conducting independent analysis — but India's regulators have heard that argument before, from Google.
carousel.image_caption: Aerial view of Apple Park in Cupertino, California — headquarters of a company now facing up to $38 billion in antitrust exposure in India
carousel.nri_angle: Indian-origin iOS developers and fintech founders on both sides of the Pacific could see fundamental changes to how the App Store operates in India, while PhonePe — widely used by NRIs for cross-border payments — is among the complainants.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: KPIT Technologies Just Lost 17% in a Single Day — and 6 Lakh Retail Investors Are Caught in the Wreckage
carousel.excerpt: The Pune-based auto software company's surprise profit warning, driven by sudden European OEM spending cuts, triggers JPMorgan downgrade and drags peers Tata Elxsi and LTTS down with it — a cautionary tale for NRI investors in India's mid-cap IT story
carousel.image_caption: A stock trading screen showing market data — KPIT Technologies shares crashed 17% to a near four-year low on July 1, 2026
carousel.nri_angle: NRI investors with exposure to Indian mid-cap IT mutual funds are directly affected — KPIT's crash reveals the concentration risk in thematic auto-tech bets and raises questions about whether the broader Indian IT services sector faces structural headwinds from European demand weakness and AI disruption
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk
